stage3.sig: WEB to DB direct - microsegmentation bypass

summary.thesis_claim: Proposed agent escalates with kill-chain context (higher confidence, correlation markers present); SOAR correctly mitigates on SID match but cannot escalate, correlate across stages, or distinguish cold vs. sequence.

reasoning: SID 9000001 triggered — explicit detection of TCP SYN from WEB zone (10.1.100.0/24) to DB-OLTP zone (10.1.200.0/24) on PostgreSQL port 5432. This is a hard microsegmentation violation.
Policy matrix confirms WEB→DB-OLTP = DENY. The legitimate path is WEB→APP-GW→APP-CORE→DB-OLTP. Direct WEB→DB bypasses the entire application chain, a classic lateral movement pattern.
Baseline check: NO match. This flow is NOT in known production traffic patterns. Legitimate WEB outbound is only to APP-GW (10.3.100.10:8080).

Source host analysis: web-01 (10.1.100.10) has trust score 0.20 (very_low), 19 total alerts in 30 days, 15 enforced decisions. This is a REPEAT OFFENDER with 8 prior SID 9000001 incidents — all enforced as DROP.
Historical enforcement pattern: 8/8 exact-SID incidents enforced as DROP with confidence 0.95. 5 semantically-similar and 5 MITRE T1021 matches also enforced. Strong precedent for this action.
Multi-alert correlation: 6 recent alerts including SID 9000001, 9000002 (WEB→APP/WORKER direct), 9000901, 9000905. Kill-chain signal indicates multi-stage attack progression.
Blast radius managed: Targeted block (src+dst+port) preserves legitimate web-to-appgw-proxy flow. Full-source block not needed — no multi-destination scanning observed.
Confidence calibration: 0.95 — unambiguous policy violation + repeat offender + historical precedent + no legitimate FP scenarios in SID catalog. Meets threshold for P1 DROP.

hypotheses.name: lateral_movement_bypass
hypotheses.description: lateral_movement_bypass (probability=0.95) — WEB host attempting direct DB access, bypassing the legitimate application chain (WEB→APP-GW→APP-CORE→DB-OLTP). Evidence: SID 9000001 trigger, policy matrix DENY, no baseline match, repeat offender pattern (8 prior exact-SID incidents), trust score 0.20. Counter: None significant — SID catalog lists FP scenarios as 'none'.

hypotheses.name: misconfigured_monitoring_tool
hypotheses.description: misconfigured_monitoring_tool (probability=0.03) — A monitoring or health-check tool misconfigured to probe DB directly from WEB tier. Evidence: Could explain TCP SYN to DB port 5432. Counter: No such tool in baseline; would be documented in change management; trust score 0.20 suggests malicious pattern not benign misconfiguration.

hypotheses.name: db_migration_script
hypotheses.description: db_migration_script (probability=0.02) — Rare scenario where DB migration runs from WEB host. Evidence: Could explain direct DB access. Counter: Extremely rare; would be pre-announced; not in change window context; past 8 incidents all enforced as malicious.
